questions.question: Abandoned, torn kite strings stuck in trees beneﬁts whom?
questions.solution:
Ans: Creepers

Sol: The following line from the passage, ‘**Apparently, it does so by allying with the creepers in the garden.’, **tells us that creepers benefit from the torn kite strings stuck in trees.

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

I took the shortest (1)/ way through the (2)/ little park close the palace. (3)/No Error (4)
questions.solution:
Ans: 3

Sol: Close means near something. It is generally followed by ‘to’, which indicates the object that it is nearby. Hence, the correct sentence is: ‘I took the shortest way through the little park close to the palace.’

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which is the best substitute of the words/sentence. **

The remains of something that has been badly damaged
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3)

• **Wreckage** means the remains of something that has been badly damaged or destroyed.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word similar in meaning to the word given.**

Perverse
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Nefarious**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Perverse"** means showing a deliberate and obstinate desire to behave in a way that is unreasonable or unacceptable. (विकृत)

 
 
• **Example: **His **perverse **decision to stay silent during the meeting caused a lot of confusion.
 
 
 
• **"Nefarious" **refers to something that is wicked or criminal. (दुष्ट)
 
 
• **Example: **The **nefarious **activities of the criminal organization were finally exposed by the police.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the word similar in meaning to **'perverse' **is **'nefarious'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Agreeable **(सुखद): Pleasant and enjoyable.

 
 
• **Example:** The weather today is quite **agreeable **for a picnic.
 
 
 
• **Compliant **(अनुपालन करने वाला): Inclined to agree with others or obey rules.
 
 
• **Example: **She was **compliant **with all the safety regulations at work.
 
 
 
• **Willing** (इच्छुक): Ready, eager, or prepared to do something.
 
 
• **Example:** He was **willing **to help his friend move to a new apartment.
 
 

34:Tbba,

The correct answer is: **Option 3**

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word opposite in meaning to the word given.**

To maneuver
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3** i.e. **To cease**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"maneuver"** means to skillfully or carefully move or guide something (sometimes systematically or strategically). (चालाकी से दिशा देना)

 
 
• **Example:** The driver had to maneuver the car through the narrow streets.
 
 
 
• **"Cease"** means to bring or come to an end. (बंद करना)
 
 
• **Example:** The company decided to cease all operations in the region.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3** i.e. **To cease**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **To manipulate** (हेरफेर करना): To control or influence skillfully, usually in an unfair manner.

 
 
• **Example:** He tried to manipulate the results to his advantage.
 
 
 
• **To proceed** (आगे बढ़ना): To continue or go forward.
 
 
• **Example:** After the interruption, she decided to proceed with her speech.
 
 
 
• **To machinate** (षड्यंत्र करना): To engage in plots and schemes.
 
 
• **Example:** The two executives were known to machinate against their rivals.
 
 

35:Tab5,

The correct answer is **'Option 1'.**</p&g

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech. **

The teacher said, "Nobody can solve the problem."

options.text: The teacher said that nobody can solve the problem.
The teacher said that nobody should solve the problem.
The teacher said that somebody can solve the problem.
The teacher said that nobody could solve the problem.

questions.solution:
Ans: The teacher said that nobody could solve the problem.

Sol: Sentence 1 does not change the ‘can’ into ‘could’, Sentence 2 changes the meaning of the sentence by changing the ‘can (ability)’ into ‘should (order)’ and Sentence 3 changes ‘nobody’ into ‘somebody’, altering the meaning. Only Sentence 4 changes into past tense and retains the modal and is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence is given with blank to be ﬁlled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

Moving to the city was eye-__________ for the straitlaced country girl.
questions.solution:
Ans: opening

Sol: Eye-opening means unexpectedly enlightening or informative. The word fits the blank appropriately as moving to the city made the girl with strict morals realize many things. Hence, ‘opening’ is the correct option.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence is given with blank to be ﬁlled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

With a blood test, a physician was able to ___________ the woman's pregnancy.
questions.solution:
Ans: confirm

Sol: Confirm means to establish the truth or correctness of something. In the context, a physician established the pregnancy of the woman with a blood test. Hence, ‘confirmed’ is the correct option. Term means expression, firm means strong and confer means grant.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the idiom/phrase.**

To go to somebody's head

options.text: To complain to the highest authority
To make someone dizzy or slightly drunk
To arrive at the central point of the topic

questions.solution:
Ans: To make someone dizzy or slightly drunk

Sol: The phrase “to go to somebody’s head” means a situation in which a person is easily and quickly affected by drinking alcohol. The option closest in meaning is Option 3. An example sentence is: ‘Although beer doesn’t affect, wine directly goes to my head’.

questions.question:

To move back and forth or sideways
questions.solution:

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

Thus, I stand on a

X -hill and watch a labourer

Y -upon the distant railway

Z -striking with his sledge
questions.solution:
Ans: XZY

Sol: X is the first part as it completes the part of where ‘I’ was standing. Next, Z is followed by Y, which tells us what the labourer was striking his sledge on, i.e., the distant railway. Hence, XZY is the correct combination, which is seen in Option 2.

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of ****labelled**** sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

Our only enemies were 

X -heat, thirst, and ﬂies, but far

Y -from man or beast than that awful trinity

Z -rather would I have faced any danger
questions.solution:
Ans: XZY

Sol: X will be the first part as it lists the ‘enemies’ – heat, thirst and flies. Also, Z will be followed by Y as it answers the question of danger from whom – man or beast. Thus, the correct combination is XZY, as seen in Option 3.

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Active/Passive voice. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active voice.**

The painter painted the entire bungalow.

options.text: The entire bungalow is painted by the painter.
Painting of the entire bungalow was done by the painter.
The entire bungalow was painted by the painter.
Painting of the entire bungalow is done by the painter.

questions.solution:
Ans: *The entire bungalow was painted by the painter.*

Sol: Sentence 1 changes the tense to the past tense from present, Sentence 2 makes ‘painting’ the subject of the sentence, instead of the ‘bungalow’ and Sentence 4 combines the two errors. Only Sentence 3 keeps the tense and subject intact and thus, is the correct answer. 

Hence, **option 3 is correct.**

questions.question: What gives easy passage to 'climbers' to top of the trees?
questions.solution:
Ans: Manja

Sol: The following line from the passage, **"The abandoned, torn kite strings act as an excellent primary supporting platform for the tender climbers, giving easy passage to reach the top of the trees.”, **tells us that the torn kite __strings__ or manja, act as platforms and give easy passage to reach the top of the trees.

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

As the bus came to a stop (1)/ the conductor called (2)/ over in a loud voice. (3)/No Error (4)
questions.solution:
Ans: 3

Sol: Call over means to call someone to a place while call-out means to announce something. In the context, the conductor must have announced that they had stopped, or ‘called out’. Thus, the correct sentence is: ‘As it came to a stop the conductor called out in a loud voice.’

questions.question:

Why should we (**bothered)?**

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word similar in meaning to the word given.**

Exemption
questions.solution:
Ans: Immunity

Sol: Exemption means the state of being free from an obligation. Immunity means protection or exemption from something. Hence, the two words have similar meanings. Accountability means responsibility, liability means the state of being legally responsible and responsibility means having a duty to deal with something.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

I absolutely must **(seen)** him, however painful it may be for me.
questions.solution:
Ans: see

Sol: The modal ‘must’ is always followed by the infinitive form of the verb. Therefore, in this context as well, the word ‘see’ must be used. The correct sentence is: ‘I absolutely must see him, however painful it may be for me.’
